briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Fight Becomes a Campaign Issue as Federal Rescheduling Clears a Legal Hurdle
briefs.top: Michigan's 24% wholesale tax is now a defining issue in the governor's race, with cannabis operators lining up behind a repeal pledge and bipartisan legislators pushing HB 6224 — real momentum for relief. Nationally, a D.C. Circuit win for medical marijuana rescheduling and accelerating FDA psychedelics pathways signal the federal landscape is bending toward opportunity even as the broader Schedule III fight grinds on.

local.text: GOP gubernatorial nominee John James is campaigning on a pledge to 'repeal or sharply reduce' the 24% wholesale tax, and Michigan cannabis operators — including JARS Cannabis executives who raised him $90,000 at a fundraiser — are rallying behind him, giving the industry real electoral leverage for 2026.

A bipartisan repeal bill, HB 6224, is now on the table in Lansing, with a Republican state representative framing the wholesale tax as an unnecessary burden — giving operators a concrete legislative vehicle to watch this fall.

Grön's bestselling 'Pearls' gummies, owned by Wyld, just landed on Michigan shelves at Pure Options, High Profile, and Lume as part of a four-state rollout — fresh proof that national edibles brands still see Michigan as a growth market worth entering.

Fields Cannary is targeting a fall opening in Muskegon for a hospitality-forward dispensary-plus-restaurant buildout, pushing the retail format further than most Michigan operators have gone — a bet on experience-driven retail even amid tax pressure.

The wholesale tax generated only about $34–37 million per quarter against a $105 million-per-quarter projection, undercutting the case for keeping the rate where it is and strengthening operators' argument for a cut or repeal as the fiscal shortfall becomes undeniable.

national.text: The D.C. Circuit rebuffed a lawsuit seeking to block medical marijuana's April 2026 Schedule III reclassification on Sept. 9, finding opponents had not demonstrated grounds to overturn it — clearing a key legal cloud and stabilizing the reform already in effect.

The DEA itself formally argued in its post-hearing brief that marijuana no longer meets the criteria for Schedule I, putting the federal government's own enforcement agency on record for full rescheduling as the case heads toward an administrative law judge's recommendation.

Compass Pathways' COMP360 psilocybin therapy hit 26-week Phase 3 durability data confirming a 'rapid onset and durable profile,' with commercial launch-readiness on track for late 2026 and a first-half-2027 launch — the psychedelics sector's most advanced approval push yet.

Vireo Growth's acquisition spree continues to reshape the MSO landscape, with its all-stock deal to buy Planet 13 adding 36 dispensaries and pushing Vireo toward roughly 265 stores across 15 states — a sign of consolidation-driven confidence even in a choppy capital environment.

FDA's newly finalized psychedelics guidance signals the agency is 'receptive' to helping companies succeed, following Trump's executive order urging an established approval path for psilocybin, MDMA, and even ibogaine — with one treating physician predicting the drug class could reshape depression treatment.
